counterfactual_missing_items: no central canal stenosis or abscess
no fracture on plain X-ray of the left hip
normal tumour markers and isotope bone scan
decisive_items: bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement
response.rationale: The final MRI directly demonstrates bilateral iliacus and iliopsoas muscle oedema with enhancement and a left-sided insertional tendinopathy, which is pathognomonic for iliopsoas tendinopathy. Other candidates either lack direct imaging support (R9, R1, R6) or are explicitly ruled out by MRI (R7, R8). C1 is a redundant completion of R5 without additional raw evidence.

rejected.why: Gout history and joint effusion are non-specific; MRI shows muscle oedema and tendinopathy, not joint involvement.
Elevated inflammatory markers and joint effusion are non-specific; MRI findings point to muscle/tendon, not synovitis.
Initial differential of epidural abscess was explicitly ruled out by MRI showing no abscess or central canal stenosis.
Redundant completion of R5; R5 already includes bilateral involvement in its raw support span.
Polymyalgia rheumatica is a possible differential but MRI shows insertional tendinopathy, which is more specific for iliopsoas tendinopathy; PMR typically shows bursitis, not tendinopathy.
Cauda equina syndrome was ruled out by MRI showing no central canal stenosis or abscess.
